review_notes:
I read the whole file. I also read the supporting definitions in TriadicCube.lean (`TriadicCube`, `cubeScaleFactor`, `cubeSet`, `openCubeSet`) and checked where `cubeShrunkSet`, `cubeBoundaryLayer` and `cubeBoundary` are used. I did not search Mathlib for the `Set.pi` / `Set.Ico` lemmas.

`cubeShrunkSet`, `cubeBoundaryLayer` and `cubeBoundary` are project-specific.
- `cubeShrunkSet` is a set-builder box that matches the style of `cubeSet` and `openCubeSet`. Writing it as `Set.pi univ (fun i => Set.Ico ..)` would be an equivalent representation, but this is a deliberate local choice. I found no duplicated API or repeated conversions that justify changing it.
- `cubeBoundary` is `cubeSet \ openCubeSet`. This is the lower faces of the half-open cube only. It is not Mathlib's `frontier`, which would also include the upper faces. The two are therefore different concepts.
- `cubeBoundaryLayer` is the cube minus the shrunk core. Mathlib has no matching concept, because `Metric.thickening` and `Metric.cthickening` are neighbourhoods outside a set, not an inner layer. I found no other competing version.

The remaining declarations are theorems, which the rubric excludes. The only exception is the theorem `BoundaryLayer.cubeScaleFactor_pos`, which is a lemma and not a competing concept. I am abstaining because I found no clear case for consolidation.
